svg.title: Three decisions: request work, CPU service, device execution
svg.desc: Address-space and readiness boundaries • teaching arrangement, not an implementation
svg.text: Three decisions: request work, CPU service, device execution
Address-space and readiness boundaries • teaching arrangement, not an implementation
1. Serving scheduler
Chooses request / phase / iteration budget
Preserves request identity and KV authority
Chosen work still needs host CPU service
2. OS schedules native threads
Each has stack, registers and instruction state
Sibling threads share process memory
Runnable does not mean running now
3. Runtime tasks and CPU capacity
Tasks may share native runtime workers
Concurrency can interleave on one CPU
SMT siblings share physical core resources
4. Device and completion boundary
Host submission → device dependencies
Completion → host reconciliation → output
Host-thread exit is not a device fence
Separate processes isolate ordinary address spaces; shared resources can still couple failure.
More threads do not automatically add capacity, preserve lifetimes or shorten request latency.
